name: The Crashbook: Where to Sleep When You Can't Go Home
author: Published by the Mutual Roof Collective, 3rd edition
description: A community zine produced by the Mutual Roof Collective, an informal network of GLMZ freelancers and sympathizers who maintain a hospitality exchange for workers between contracts, in medical recovery, fleeing dangerous situations, or otherwise without stable housing. The third edition, identified by a hand-stamped red number on the back cover, is wider in scope than the previous two and includes new listings in the Harrow Stack and East Narrows. Circulated physically through dead drop distribution points and a small number of sympathetic vendors. No digital version exists by collective policy.
body:
THE CRASHBOOK
Where to Sleep When You Can't Go Home
3rd Edition — Mutual Roof Collective
Don't photograph this. Don't post it. Pass it to someone who needs it.

---

A NOTE FROM THE EDITOR

We started this because Fen Okoro had nowhere to go after her knee got rebuilt and she couldn't do stairs for six weeks and her bunk contract required her to be mobile. That was four years ago. Fen now runs the Sixteenth Stack exchange herself. This is what the network does — it turns people who needed it into people who keep it running.

This edition has seventeen active listings. We lost two from the second edition (the Pell Street sublet in Harrow collapsed structurally, everyone got out, no casualties; the Cutter's Row arrangement ended when the host family relocated to Upper Narrows after their eldest got a Tier 3 work placement — good for them, genuinely). We've added six new listings including two with medical recovery accommodation.

Before the listings: a word about Celdric Maus, property manager for Vanthorn Residential Holdings, Sixteenth and Morrow, Harrow Stack Level 4. In February he reported a freelancer — I am not printing her name, she asked me not to — to Arcturus Civil Security for "unlicensed residential subletting" after she'd stayed three nights in a unit hosted by a friend of the network. Three nights. She was post-job, processing a shoulder replacement, had nowhere else to go. Arcturus came. You know what Arcturus coming looks like.

Celdric Maus does not deserve a warning. He deserves to know that the network knows his name, his schedule, and which units in his building host people he'd like to report. We are not threatening him. We are informing him that the informal economy he profits from — freelancers who pay his building's corner market, freelancers who fix what his maintenance staff won't, freelancers who quietly keep Harrow Stack functional — we are all aware of what he did. Some of us have long memories and legal access to public-facing commercial spaces.

Do not use Vanthorn Residential Holdings. Tell your people.

---

THE LISTINGS

All contact via physical drop or verified vouch-chain only. No direct BCI pings to listed contacts. No screenshots. You break this, you burn the listing for everyone.

**SIXTEENTH STACK EXCHANGE — Harrow Stack, Level 7, Sixteenth Corridor**
Contact: Ask for "the Fen arrangement" at the Sixteenth Street bodega (Marra's, red awning, cash only)
Capacity: 2-3 persons, rotating
Duration: Up to 12 nights, extensions negotiable by host
Notes: Accessible unit available for mobility-limited recovery. No stairwell required. Hosts ask for one small contribution to the communal supply box per stay (non-cash, think: food, medical consumables, batteries, sealant tape). No active contracts running through the space — if you're hot, say so upfront and they'll route you elsewhere.

*"I stayed at Sixteenth for nine days after Millhaven. I couldn't hold a spoon. They fed me anyway and didn't ask about the job. I've sent four people there since." — C.V., B-tier, East Narrows*

**THE LIBRARY — Cutter's District, Lower Narrows, Voss Building Basement**
Contact: Drop a note in the third ventilation panel left of the Voss Building service entrance. Mark it with a blue edge.
Capacity: 4, sleeping bags and floor pads, two cots
Duration: 3-7 nights standard
Notes: No power draws over 200w. The basement hosts are not freelancers — they are civilians who believe in the network. Treat the space accordingly. No weapons cleaning on premises. No loud arguments after 22:00. Someone left a blood-soaked jacket there in October and the hosts nearly shut the whole thing down. If you are actively injured, say so BEFORE arriving so they can prepare.

**MIRA'S SECOND ROOM — East Narrows, Breck Terrace Level 12, Unit 1204**
Contact: Vouch-chain only. Minimum two vouches from B-tier or above.
Capacity: 1 person
Duration: Flexible, discussed with host
Notes: Mira is a retired logistics coordinator, not a freelancer. She has a spare room. She offers it because her son used the network before he was killed on a job three years ago. Please understand what that means before you stay there. Be a person in her home, not a package being stored.

*"I want people to know this resource exists and I want people to know I will absolutely be checking your vouches. My son's name was Davan. He was twenty-six. He fixed machines and made good tea and he got betrayed by a broker who sold his route. I'm not a charity. I'm his mother doing something with the grief." — Mira, listed by request*

**THE STACKS AT IRONTON — Ironton Shelf, Column C, Floors 14-17**
Contact: Ask at the Ironton Column C resident board (physical board, lobby level) for the "neighbor rotation"
Capacity: Varies week to week, usually 1-2
Duration: Up to 5 nights
Notes: This is a resident-run informal exchange among people who live in Column C. Freelancers from outside the building are welcome but you are a guest in someone's home. The column has a high density of unaugmented residents. Do not activate visible chrome in common areas without asking first — not because it's wrong, but because some of the elderly residents have trauma responses and the network has agreed to respect that.

---

ETIQUETTE: WHAT YOU OWE AND WHAT YOU DON'T

What you owe:
— Honesty about your situation upfront. If you're being looked for, say so. If you're injured, say so. If you're carrying something that could put the host at risk, say so or don't come.
— Leave the space cleaner than you found it. This is not negotiable. This is not "if you feel like it."
— A contribution of some kind, calibrated to what you have. If you have nothing, say so. Hosts understand nothing — they have all been nothing at some point. What they don't understand is nothing offered while you have something to offer.
— Tell us when a listing needs to be updated. Hosts move. Situations change. A bad update costs someone a safe night.

What you don't owe:
— Your real name
— Details about your work
— Conversation beyond common courtesy
— A timeline of your next contract

What gets you blacklisted (this list is real, these are things that happened):
— Bringing Arcturus to a host's door, for any reason, in any form
— Using a listing address as a contract delivery point without explicit host permission
— Stealing from hosts. One person did this. We know who. They will never sleep safe in this network again and that information has been passed up and down every vouch chain we have.
— Reporting a listing to a landlord or property authority (see: Celdric Maus, above)
— Using a host's BCI hardware without asking
— Leaving someone else's dependent — child, elder, recovery patient — unsupported when you were the only one present

---

A THANK-YOU NOTE

*We received this in the drop box at Marra's bodega. We are printing it in full with permission.*

To whoever keeps this thing running —

I came off a job in November with a cracked orbital socket and Φ14 in my account and I did not know about the network. A woman at the Voss Building service entrance — I don't know her name, she didn't give it — saw me sitting on the curb and handed me a second edition Crashbook with two listings circled. I stayed at Sixteenth for eleven days. They held my hand through the bone-knit swelling. They made me eat. They did not ask what happened.

I was going to sleep in the Ironton corridor that first night. I know what happens to people who sleep in the Ironton corridor.

I'm B-tier now. I have a bunk contract. I've passed this zine to four people. One of them sent me a note saying it saved her. So that's five of us walking around because someone decided to make a list.

I don't know what else to say. Thank you is not enough but it's what I have.

— Name withheld, Narrows district

---

NEXT EDITION
If you host or know a host willing to be listed, drop a note at any of the collection points marked in the network. If you have updates to existing listings, same. If you just want to help and don't know how, buy something at Marra's and tell them the Collective sent you.

We take care of each other because no one else does. That's not a slogan. That's just what's true.

— The Editor, Mutual Roof Collective
*Third Edition. Printed at an undisclosed location on recycled thermal stock. No digital archive.*
